newsitem.title: USA: US SEPT S&PS END LOWER, COLLAPSE LATE WITH T-BONDS.
newsitem.headline: US SEPT S&PS END LOWER, COLLAPSE LATE WITH T-BONDS.

text.p: U.S. September Standard & Poor's 500 futures ended sharply lower, collapsing in sloppy, active pit trade after U.S. T-bond prices sold off late in the day, traders and analysts said.
"We've had big gaps in bid and offers," one trader said. "There have been big spreads -- more than usual. It's just a very disjointed trade, very sloppy."

September S&Ps breezed through support at 961.50, 959.50 and 957.50, as U.S. T-bond futures sold off into their close at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT. Afterwards, September S&Ps jerked lower to 954.25, near Wednesday's low of 953.70.

Earlier in the day, September S&Ps set a record high of 969.20, but found enough profit-taking to keep the contract from staging another run-up to a psychological resistance level of 970.00 and chart objectives at 972.25 and 972.50.
"Locals have been tromping on it all day, looking for sell-stop orders," another floor trader said.
However, the profit-taking selloff did not become convincing until after midday.
U.S. September T-bond futures quickly sold off after rising in reaction to the results of the 30-year T-bond auction.

Analysts said a combination of technicals and comments from Kansas City Federal Reserve president Thomas Hoenig may have accelerated U.S. T-bonds' slide. Hoenig said upside inflation risks exist in the U.S. economy given the low jobless rate. He also said central bankers need to be cautious about inflation.
The T-bond sell-off filtered into the S&P pit in a matter of minutes, creating a disorderly market, S&P traders said.
"Every day everyone is expecting the end of the world," one trader said, referring to expectations for a steep market correction.
"We've had some nasty trades today, but I can't get too worked up over this," he said. "We got rid of a lot of weak shorts."
Fair value for September was at 4.37 points to cash, with arbitrage buy programs seen at a premium of 5.50 points and arbitrage sell programs at 3.50 over.

At the end of pit trade, September S&Ps were 7.35 points lower at 956.25, KCBT Value Lines were off 5.20 lower at 848.00, Nikkeis were 475 lower at 19,310, Midcap 400s were 3.75 lower at 317.50, Nasdaq 100s were down 7.75 at 1,141.00 and Russell 2000s were 0.75 lower at 421.50.
